questions.question: We use only 10% of our brains when learning.
questions.answer: False - Brain imaging studies show that we use all parts of our brain, even when at rest. Learning engages multiple areas of the brain.

questions.question: Intelligence is fixed from birth and cannot be changed.
questions.answer: False - Intelligence is not fixed; it can develop through learning, effort, and experience. The brain has neuroplasticity, allowing it to adapt over time.

questions.question: People learn best when taught in their preferred learning style (visual, auditory, kinesthetic).
questions.answer: False - Research shows that using multiple learning methods is more effective than relying on a single 'learning style.'

questions.question: Multitasking improves efficiency by helping the brain process multiple pieces of information at once.
questions.answer: False - Studies show that multitasking reduces focus and increases cognitive load, making learning less effective.

questions.question: Memory is like a recording that perfectly stores everything we learn.
questions.answer: False - Memory is reconstructive, meaning it changes over time and is influenced by emotions, experiences, and context.

questions.question: Cramming the night before an exam is an effective way to retain information long-term.
questions.answer: False - Cramming may help with short-term recall, but spaced repetition is much more effective for long-term retention.

questions.question: The brain is fully developed by the time a person turns 18.
questions.answer: False - Brain development, especially in areas responsible for decision-making and impulse control, continues into the mid-20s.

questions.question: Spaced repetition helps reinforce learning over time.
questions.answer: True - Repeating information over spaced intervals strengthens memory retention and reduces forgetting.

questions.question: Mistakes are an essential part of the learning process.
questions.answer: True - Learning from mistakes helps build understanding and improves problem-solving skills.

questions.question: Neuroplasticity allows the brain to rewire and adapt to new learning.
questions.answer: True - The brain is capable of forming new neural connections throughout life, enabling learning and adaptation.
